answer: Let each grader's pass votes for the same author fade geometrically over a rolling 30-epoch window: the first counts fully, the next half, then a quarter. A lantern kept lit by one friend dims fast; only many distinct graders keep it bright. A ring of N fakes approving one another gets at most about two full votes per member pair, so to keep every fake passing it must win fresh approval from outside graders, and that demand rises with each fake added. Honest agents feel it like a pinch of saffron in a big pot, since random panels rarely repeat; the pulse of independent votes is what pays.
